title: Invariant CANON: every request identity has exactly one canonicalizing owner in the core; authz, routing, cache keys, logging, upstream forwarding and handlers consume only that canonical value
summary: Statement for SPEC_INVARIANTS. CANON-1 single owner: for each identity kind K (route path, query, host/authority, TLS server name, origin, header field set, cookie jar, media type, JSON body, principal/tenant id) exactly one core function canon_K: Raw -> Result<Canon_K, Reject> exists; no other module may parse Raw_K. CANON-2 reject, don't repair: canon_K returns Reject (400/421/415) for any input with more than one plausible reading under the parsers listed in the owner table (encoded '/', '\\', ';', '%00', dot segments, empty segments, non-ASCII, duplicate singleton fields, duplicate JSON names, duplicate cookie names, lone surrogates, out-of-range numbers, miscapitalized cookie prefixes). Repair is allowed only for the RFC 3986 6.2.2 safe set (decode unreserved, uppercase hex, lowercase scheme/host, strip default port, strip trailing slash) and only when CANON-4 holds. CANON-3 type sealing: Canon_K values are newtypes with private constructors; the raw bytes are reachable only through an explicit RawFor<Signature> capability (webhook HMAC, RFC 9421) that is not accepted by authz or routing APIs. CANON-4 forward what you checked: anything sent upstream or written to a store is re-serialized from Canon_K, never forwarded raw (Cloudflare's default 'normalize incoming ON / to-origin OFF' is the counterexample). CANON-5 decide on the router's output: authorization keys on the matched route id + typed params produced by the single router, never re-matches path strings. CANON-6 cross-layer binding: TLS SNI, :authority/Host and Origin are each canonicalized and must map to the same vhost/trust config or the request is 421 (RFC 9113 8.3.1). CANON-7 idempotence and agreement: canon_K(serialize(canon_K(x))) == canon_K(x), and every consumer parser in the golden build, fed serialize(canon_K(x)), yields the same identity (checked by the CI gate). CANON-8 upstream profile: when an upstream applies its own folding (case-insensitive paths, Windows trailing dot/backslash, Rails format suffix), its profile is declared in config and canon_K applies the same folding or rejects; undeclared upstreams default to the strictest profile.
specifics: Derived from 30+ dated instances (r4e07.instance-ledger) and the executed differential (r4e07.diff-corpus-executed, r4e07.canon-ref-zero-disagreement). Clause-to-instance map: CANON-1 grpc-go CVE-2026-33186, s3-proxy CVE-2026-42882; CANON-2 Quarkus CVE-2026-50559 (incomplete-fix lineage after CVE-2026-39852), Heimdall CVE-2026-42272; CANON-3 Hono CVE-2026-39410; CANON-4 Cloudflare normalization defaults, paivana commit; CANON-5 axum #2678 + executed matchit '/admin/' miss; CANON-6 Traefik CVE-2026-48491/53622, Jetty CVE-2026-6790, Pingora CVE-2026-105298; CANON-7 canonicalizer self-bug caught by differential; CANON-8 '/ADMIN', '/admin.' residuals.
overclaim_risk: Invariant statement is E until mechanized; the executed corpus is small (49 paths, 36 hosts, 25 JSON docs) and adversarially chosen, so 'zero disagreement after canonicalization' is a demonstration on that corpus, not a proof over all inputs.
underclaim_risk: Reject-don't-repair is sometimes dismissed as breaking clients; the instance record shows nearly every 2026 bypass came from a repair step (decode, trim, merge) done in one component and not another, and browsers already send canonical forms for paths.

title: Owner table: identity -> canonicalizing component -> consumers -> reject rule (golden build)
summary: ROUTE PATH -> core::canon::path (origin-form only; decode unreserved only; reject %2F %5C %3B %00 %25-non-hex, literal '\\' ';' non-ASCII, '.'/'..' segments, empty segments; strip trailing slash with 308) -> router (matchit on canonical string), authz (route id), response cache key, access log, upstream request line (re-serialized). QUERY -> core::canon::query (application/x-www-form-urlencoded strict: '&' only, ';' not a separator [python-multipart CVE-2026-53538], duplicate keys rejected unless the route declares a list param) -> handler extractors, cache key. HOST/AUTHORITY -> core::canon::authority (ASCII lowercase, default port stripped, trailing dot rejected, IPv4 only canonical dotted-quad, then EXACT lookup in configured A-label vhost set; no IDNA on ingress) -> vhost select, authz, cache key, upstream Host/:authority (re-serialized, Host header rewritten to equal :authority). TLS SNI -> listener (rustls ClientHello server_name, ASCII lowercase) -> cert select; bound to authority by CANON-6. ORIGIN -> core::canon::origin (strict serialized-origin parse; compare tuple to allowlist of configured tuples; 'null' never allowed with credentials; no regex) -> CORS, CSRF, WS upgrade gate. HEADER SET -> core::canon::headers (names lowercased by http crate; singleton fields Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, Authorization, :authority duplicates rejected 400; Host!=:authority 400; obs-fold/obs-text rejected) -> all. COOKIES -> core::canon::cookies (RFC 6265bis-22 algorithm, strip SP/HTAB only, duplicate names rejected, case-variant __Host-/__Secure- rejected, nameless rejected) -> session layer only (handlers receive typed session, never the jar). MEDIA TYPE -> core::canon::media_type (strict token/token; duplicate parameters rejected; unparseable -> 415; essence compared after ASCII lowercase) -> body codec registry selection, CSRF policy. JSON BODY -> core::codec::json (I-JSON RFC 7493: duplicate names reject, lone surrogates reject, integers outside +-(2^53-1) reject or route-declared decimal string, non-finite reject, BOM reject) -> policy engine input and handler deserialization from the SAME parsed value (one parse, two consumers). PRINCIPAL/TENANT ID -> core::canon::ident (ASCII slug [a-z0-9-] for tenant ids; external usernames via PRECIS UsernameCaseMapped RFC 8265 at registration and login with the same function) -> authz, DB gate (bound parameters compared under COLLATE "C" / bytewise, per irl-pg-collation-cex), logs.
specifics: Crate placement: one crate aegis-canon (no I/O, forbid(unsafe_code)), depends only on http 1.5.0, percent-encoding 2.3.2, serde_json 1.0.154 (with a custom duplicate-rejecting visitor; serde_json Value is last-wins by default); does NOT depend on url (WHATWG semantics, intended for browsers/clients) for ingress; url 2.5.8 is used only for egress/SSRF URL parsing and Origin parsing where WHATWG semantics match what browsers send. simd-json and sonic-rs are excluded from the golden build (first-wins duplicates; simd-json lone-surrogate bug).
overclaim_risk: Placement choices are mine; not benchmarked for cost (copy/allocation of canonical strings).
underclaim_risk: One may think a typed canonical layer is novel and risky; Envoy (normalize_path, merge_slashes, path_with_escaped_slashes_action=REJECT_REQUEST) and Cloudflare (URL normalization) already ship the path part at hyperscale.

title: EXECUTED cross-crate differential: one corpus fed to url/http/fluent-uri/matchit/idna/serde_json/simd-json/sonic-rs/cookie/mime/httparse + CPython 3.12.9 stdlib; disagreement counts per pair
summary: Harness: 07-work/diffh (Rust, rustc 1.88.0, built under heavy.sh in 45 s, target 185 MB deleted after run) + analyze.py (python3 -I). Versions: url 2.5.8, http 1.5.0, idna 1.1.0, fluent-uri 0.3.2, matchit 0.8.6, serde_json 1.0.154, simd-json 0.15.1 (MSRV-resolved; same code path in 0.18.1), sonic-rs 0.5.10, cookie 0.18.2, mime 0.3.17, httparse 1.10.1, unicode-normalization 0.1.26. Results (recomputed): WPT urltestdata @c48d5874 (2026-09-19) 896 cases: url passes 831; on 145 base-less special-scheme URLs that url accepts, http::Uri rejects 43, gives a different path on 25 of the remaining 102 and a different host on 5; CPython urlsplit host differs on 9. Of 207 inputs the WHATWG standard calls invalid, http::Uri accepts 67, fluent-uri 110, urlsplit 173. PATHS (49 adversarial request targets, decision 'is /admin'): admin count ranges from 7 (matchit on raw path, axum's behaviour) to 25 (CPython normpath(unquote)); pairwise disagreements: raw vs WHATWG 14, raw vs decode-then-dot 17, raw vs CPython 19, matchit raw vs matchit on WHATWG path 15, decode-only vs matchit-on-url 20; only 2 of 28 non-degenerate pairs disagree <=2 times. HOSTS (36): pairwise value disagreements 4-24 (url vs ascii-lower 24, idna_strict vs urlsplit 24); 'is example.com' decision disagreements up to 11. IdnaTestV2 (WPT, 2,674 usable): url host 1,916 pass, idna::domain_to_ascii 1,917; CPython IDNA2003 codec agrees on 1,463. JSON (25 docs, value of 'role'): serde_json Value last-wins, serde derive rejects duplicate field, simd-json and sonic-rs get() return FIRST, CPython last-wins -> pairwise disagreements 2-10; 1e400 rejected by serde Value but accepted by serde derive when the field is ignored; simd-json rejects integers > u64 without a feature flag; -0 -> -0.0 (serde), 0 (simd), 0.0 (sonic), 0 (CPython). COOKIES (20 headers, __Host-sid value): cookie crate keeps both duplicates (app picks first or last), CPython SimpleCookie last-wins: first-vs-last disagreements 4-5. CONTENT-TYPE (25): mime rejects 13 that CPython email accepts; is-JSON decision disagrees on 4-6 per pair; duplicate boundary/charset params accepted by mime with get_param = FIRST. ORIGIN (20, allow == https://example.com): raw string vs WHATWG origin 11 disagreements, WHATWG vs CPython 3 ('https://example.com\\@evil.com' -> url: example.com, urlsplit: evil.com; fullwidth host; %2e). HEADERS: httparse accepts duplicate Host, duplicate unequal Content-Length (5 and 6) and conflicting Transfer-Encoding; http::HeaderMap::get returns the first value.
specifics: Files: /home/patrickd/aegis/research/state/raw/round-004/07-work/diffh/src/main.rs, mkcorpus.py, corpus/corpus.json, analyze.py, rust_out.json, results.json, summary.txt. Hardware i9-14900HX laptop, Linux 6.17. Reproduce: heavy.sh cargo build --release; ./diffh/target/release/diffh corpus > rust_out.json; python3 -I analyze.py rust_out.json corpus/corpus.json corpus/IdnaTestV2.clean.json results.json.
overclaim_risk: Counts depend on corpus choice: the path/host/JSON corpora are hand-built adversarial sets, so counts are 'distinct divergences found', not rates in real traffic. The 'is /admin' decision function is mine.
underclaim_risk: Every pair of independently written parsers disagreed somewhere on a 49-item corpus; real ecosystems chain 3-5 such parsers per request.

title: EXECUTED: a strict reject-don't-repair reference canonicalizer drives pairwise parser disagreement on accepted inputs from 331/331/69 to 0/0/0 (paths/hosts/JSON); it also had its own bug, found by the same differential
summary: canon_ref.py (spec-by-code; CPython stdlib only) applied to the same corpus. Acceptance: paths 10/49, hosts 7/36, cookie headers 9/20, JSON docs 9/25, tenant slugs 5/26. The accepted canonical forms were fed back through every Rust parser and CPython: summed pairwise disagreements fell from 331 to 0 across 9 path interpreters (6 unique canonical paths), from 331 to 0 across 7 host interpreters (6 unique), and from 69 to 0 across 5 JSON parsers (9 docs). The first version of the canonicalizer accepted '0x7f.0.0.1' as a DNS name; the WHATWG url crate read it as 127.0.0.1 and the differential flagged it. Fixed with the WHATWG 'ends in a number' rule. Residual after canonicalization: '/ADMIN' and '/admin.' are canonical but an upstream with case-insensitive or Windows path semantics would read them as /admin, so CANON-8 (declared upstream profile) is needed.
overclaim_risk: Zero is on a tiny accepted set (6 to 9 values per kind). The rejection rates (80% of paths) are against an adversarial corpus and say nothing about false rejects on real traffic (see r4e07.spike-false-reject-rate).
underclaim_risk: The self-bug shows the instrument finds bugs that review misses, as irl-l5-differential-oracle-harness found for SQL lowering.

title: One mechanism, 11 instance classes, 34 dated instances (2017-2026): the component that authorizes and the one that acts canonicalize identity differently
summary: All ids OSV/GHSA-verified 2026-10-25 unless marked. (1) URL parser differential: Tsai BH USA 2017 lineage; Claroty+Snyk Jan 2022 (16 parsers, 8 CVEs); CPython CVE-2023-24329 (2023-02-17, leading blanks); WHATWG URL issue #893 (closed 2026-01-03, SSRF from spec-mandated repair) [read]; executed backslash case still live in CPython 3.12.9. (2) Percent-decoding / dot-segment before routing: Envoy CVE-2021-29492; opa-envoy-plugin CVE-2026-26205 (2026-02-19, double slash); Heimdall CVE-2026-42272 (2026-05-08, %2f vs %2F); s3-proxy CVE-2026-42882 (2026-05-11, RequestURI vs Path); @fastify/middie CVE-2026-14198 (2026-07-01); Quarkus CVE-2026-50559 (2026-07-29, %3B/%2F/%5C, incomplete fix of CVE-2026-39852); Envoy CVE-2026-73553 path-param canonicalization (2026-08-26, in rec60 node); axum #2678 open since 2024-03-25. (3) IDNA/Unicode host folding: idna CVE-2024-12224 / RUSTSEC-2024-0421 (2024-12-09, fixed 1.0.0); Go x/net/idna CVE-2026-39821 (2026-05-22); WHATWG PR #914 (merged 2026-06-25) reverses strictness for ASCII xn-- labels; rust-url #1135 open. (4) SNI vs Host vs :authority: Traefik CVE-2026-48491 and CVE-2026-53622 (both 2026-06-23); Jetty CVE-2026-6790 (2026-07-14); Netty CVE-2026-59900 (2026-07-29); Pingora CVE-2026-105298 (2026-10-20). (5) Header name case / duplicates: grpc-go CVE-2026-84303 (2026-09-01, mixed-case RBAC header match); libsoup CVE-2025-14523 duplicate Host (AlmaLinux patch; not in OSV) [C]; Netty CVE-2026-59900; executed httparse/HeaderMap behaviour. (6) gRPC :path canonical route: grpc-go CVE-2026-33186 (2026-03-18, fixed 1.79.3). (7) JSON duplicate keys / numbers: CouchDB CVE-2017-12635 (Erlang vs JS parser 'roles'); Bitcoin Core #20949 (JSON-RPC proxy); Bishop Fox 49-parser survey; Go encoding/json v1 case-insensitive + last-wins (Trail of Bits 2025-06-17); Cpanel::JSON::XS CVE-2026-9334 (2026-06-03); simd-json #481 (2026-09-22, open). (8) Cookie name prefixes / parsing: PHP CVE-2020-7070; Werkzeug CVE-2023-23934; Hono CVE-2026-39410 (2026-04-08, NBSP trim); Cookie Crumbles USENIX Sec 2023 (12 CVEs); cookie-rs 0.18.2 NBSP trim (this round, executed, unreported). (9) Content-Type parameters: Fastify CVE-2022-41919; Rack CVE-2026-26961 (2026-04-02, duplicate boundary); ModSecurity CVE-2026-52747 (2026-07-10); python-multipart CVE-2026-53538 (2026-06-22). (10) Origin / trailing dot / port: jupyter-server CVE-2026-40110 (2026-05-05, unanchored regex); Litestar CVE-2026-25478 (2026-02-09); curl CVE-2026-8924 (2026-07-03, trailing-dot super cookie); curl CVE-2022-30115 (HSTS trailing dot). (11) Tenant/user id case folding and collation: Snipe-IT CVE-2026-86770 (2026-09-09, SAML username collation); Logto CVE-2026-15617 (2026-07-23, CVSS 9.1); prompts.chat CVE-2026-22665 (2026-04-03); PG nondeterministic ICU collation (irl-pg-collation-cex).
specifics: 2026 alone: 24 of the 34 instances are dated 2026-01..2026-10, spread over Go, Java, JS/TS, Python, Ruby, C and Rust (Pingora). Fix state on main: all CVE items have fixed versions per OSV except simd-json #481 (open, PR #482 open), cookie-rs NBSP (unreported), rust-url #1135 (open), axum #2678 (open, feature request), Logto CVE-2026-15617 (no fix recorded at publication).
overclaim_risk: Severity varies widely (CVSS 3.7 to 9.8). Several are configuration-dependent (Traefik wildcard+mTLS; Rack needs a first-wins WAF in front).
underclaim_risk: Only instances with a CVE or an issue are counted. Cloudflare's own docs show the default config has rules and origin seeing different paths, which is a standing instance with no CVE.

title: WHATWG URL PR #914 (merged 2026-06-25) makes ASCII hosts with invalid xn-- labels pass through lowercased; rust-url 2.5.8 / idna 1.1.0 still reject them (758/2,674 IdnaTestV2 rows, 8 urltestdata rows)
summary: PR #914 'Add Unicode ToASCII fallback for ASCII domains': when ToASCII fails, the domain is all ASCII and has no forbidden code points, return the lowercased domain (motivated by real sites such as xn--...blogspot.com). WPT commit b63305b743 (2026-06-25) 'IDNA cannot fail ASCII domains, even if they start with xn--' regenerated IdnaTestV2.json and urltestdata.json. Executed: url 2.5.8 fails exactly these rows (all 758 IdnaTestV2 misses are expected-value/got-reject). servo/rust-url #1135 (hsivonen, 2026-06-24, open): idna 'will need major changes'; no time before August. Last rust-url release on crates.io: 2.5.8 (2026-01-05). Main has later fixes (caret percent-encoding #1141, 2026-07-08; file: drive-letter host #1127, 2026-07-31). Implementation bugs filed for Gecko, WebKit, Deno, Node. Security reading: this is NOT a collision (the passthrough keeps 'xn--example-.com' distinct from 'example.com', unlike CVE-2024-12224), but browsers and rust-url now disagree on accept/reject for a class of hosts. Direction is fail-closed on the Rust side, so it is a compatibility issue for AEGIS, not a bypass.
specifics: Other url 2.5.8 vs current WPT gaps (65 urltestdata failures): about 40 file: cases, 5 opaque-path trailing spaces, 7 '///x' relative to a special base (url rejects; spec resolves to host x), 3 backslash-in-non-special (url turns '\\/a' against foo://foo/a into host 'a'; spec keeps it as path), 2 caret encoding (fixed on main).
overclaim_risk: Impact for a server is limited: AEGIS ingress should not run IDNA on Host at all (r4e07.ingress-host-exact-match).
underclaim_risk: It is a live, dated example that the WHATWG standard itself moves monthly, so a pinned url crate drifts from browsers.

title: Rust JSON parsers disagree on duplicate names: serde_json Value last-wins, serde derive rejects, simd-json and sonic-rs return the first; simd-json 0.15-0.18.1 decodes a lone high surrogate to U+0000 (issue #481 open)
summary: Executed (r4e07.diff-corpus-executed). For {"role":"user","role":"admin"}: serde_json::Value -> admin, #[derive(Deserialize)] -> error 'duplicate field', simd_json OwnedValue.get -> user (both pairs kept, re-serialized with both), sonic_rs::Value.get -> user (both kept), CPython json -> admin. So a policy check on simd-json/sonic-rs and a handler on serde_json read different roles from one body (the CouchDB CVE-2017-12635 shape). simd-json: get_unicode_codepoint returns Ok((0, offset)) for a high surrogate not followed by \\u, a leftover 'bytes written = 0 means failure' sentinel; '\\ud800' becomes '\\0'. Reported as simd-lite/simd-json #481 (2026-09-22) with fix PR #482, both open; code unchanged on main as fetched 2026-10-25. Related: #457 (closed 2026-07-05) parse_str UTF-8 soundness advisory. Numbers: serde_json Value rejects 1e400, but a derived struct that ignores the field accepts it; simd-json rejects integers > u64 by default; -0 has four different representations across the parsers.
specifics: L5 rule: one parse per body in the core codec with a duplicate-rejecting visitor (serde_json with a custom MapAccess visitor, or serde derive's built-in duplicate-field error for fixed schemas). Policy engine and handler receive the same parsed value. simd-json and sonic-rs are excluded from the golden lockfile by cargo-deny bans until #481 is fixed and duplicate handling is configurable. I-JSON (RFC 7493) is the normative profile.
overclaim_risk: sonic-rs first-wins is documented behaviour, not a bug; risk materializes only when two parsers are mixed.
underclaim_risk: Mixing a fast parser at the edge (WAF/policy) with serde in the handler is a common performance pattern.

title: cookie crate 0.18.2 (and master) trims cookie names with str::trim(), so a browser cookie named '\\u00a0__Host-sid' (no prefix protection) is read as '__Host-sid': the Hono CVE-2026-39410 class, unreported in Rust
summary: Executed: Cookie::split_parse('\\u00a0__Host-sid=evil') yields name '__Host-sid'. Source: parse.rs line 115 (0.18.2) / 117 (master) uses key_value[..i].trim(); Rust str::trim strips Unicode White_Space, including U+00A0, U+0085, U+2000-U+200A, U+3000. RFC 6265bis-22 parse algorithm strips only leading/trailing WSP (SP/HTAB), and per the Hono advisory browsers keep U+00A0 in the name, so the browser does not apply __Host- rules to that cookie (no Secure/Path=/ /no-Domain checks), while the server treats it as prefix-protected. A cookie set by a sibling subdomain or over plain HTTP can then shadow or fixate the session. CPython SimpleCookie drops the NBSP-prefixed name. Separately, the crate keeps duplicate names, and which one the app reads (first or last) is the app's choice: executed disagreement 4/20 between first and last.
specifics: Browser-side behaviour (NBSP kept in the cookie name, prefix not enforced) is taken from the Hono advisory, not re-tested in a browser here (grade B for the end-to-end exploit, A for the parser behaviour). Mitigation in AEGIS: core::canon::cookies uses the 6265bis algorithm with SP/HTAB trimming and rejects names with non-token bytes, rejects duplicates and miscapitalized prefixes. Disclosure to rwf2/cookie-rs is for the operator to decide; no report filed by this explorer.
overclaim_risk: Exploitation needs an attacker able to set cookies for the site (sibling subdomain, MITM over HTTP, or XSS on a related origin): the same precondition prefixes are meant to defend against.
underclaim_risk: Rocket and many axum apps use this crate; the bug is in the default parse path.

title: hyper 1.12.0 / h2 0.4.20 never compare Host with :authority and do not reject duplicate Host on HTTP/1.1, so the Pingora CVE-2026-105298 / Jetty CVE-2026-6790 class exists in a bare hyper stack unless the core owns it
summary: Source read: h2 0.4.20 server.rs converts :authority into uri.authority and leaves any Host header in the HeaderMap untouched; there is no comparison. hyper 1.12.0 proto/h1/role.rs has no HOST handling (no 400 on missing or duplicate Host, which RFC 9112 3.2 requires). Executed: httparse 1.10.1 returns both Host lines; HeaderMap::get gives the first. RFC 9113 8.3.1: servers SHOULD treat Host differing from :authority as malformed; non-origin servers MUST apply scheme-based normalization before comparing. Netty CVE-2026-59900 shows the h2-to-h1 translation step is where a second Host gets through. AEGIS rule: core::canon::authority runs once per exchange for h1/h2/h3. h1: exactly one Host else 400. h2/h3: :authority required for non-CONNECT; if Host is present it must canonicalize equal, else 400. The Host header is then removed and regenerated from the canonical authority on any upstream hop.
specifics: Extends crs-l5-keying-table (which states the :authority/SNI 421 rule) with code-level evidence that the chosen HTTP stack does not supply it. Regression tests: (a) h1 two Host lines -> 400; (b) h2 :authority=a, host=b -> 400; (c) h2 :authority=A.example:443 with host=a.example -> accepted (scheme-normalized equal); (d) h2 without :authority but with host -> 400 (golden profile).
overclaim_risk: Whether hyper intends to leave this to applications is a design choice, not a bug; impact depends on what the app reads.
underclaim_risk: axum/tower apps commonly read the Host header for tenant routing while the router uses uri.authority.

title: mime 0.3.17 (last release 2023-03-20) accepts duplicate Content-Type parameters and returns the first; Rack used the last (CVE-2026-26961), so a mime-based component and a last-wins component see different multipart boundaries
summary: Executed: 'multipart/form-data; boundary=aaa; boundary=bbb' -> mime ok, get_param(boundary)=aaa, params() lists both; also with case-variant 'BOUNDARY'; charset duplicates likewise. CPython email also returns the first. Rack before 2.2.23/3.1.21/3.2.6 used a greedy regex (last boundary), letting a first-wins WAF inspect a different body (GHSA-vgpv-f759-9wx3). mime also rejects 13 of 25 Content-Type values that CPython accepts (leading space, trailing tab, ';;', ' ;charset'). Rule: core::canon::media_type rejects duplicate parameter names (case-insensitive) with 415/400.

title: 2026 cluster: TLS-layer identity (SNI) and HTTP-layer identity (Host/:authority) canonicalized by different code -> mTLS and host-ACL bypass (Traefik x2, Jetty, Netty, Pingora)
summary: Traefik CVE-2026-53622: the QUIC handshake looked up TLSOptions by exact, case-sensitive SNI; wildcard and case variants fell back to a default without client-cert requirements. Traefik CVE-2026-48491: SNICheck (the domain-fronting guard) used exact map lookups and ignored wildcard TLSOptions. Both fixed in 3.7.3 (2026-06-23). Jetty CVE-2026-6790 (2026-07-14): no authority==Host check on h1/h2/h3. Netty CVE-2026-59900 (2026-07-29): h2->h1 translation does not deduplicate Host. Pingora CVE-2026-105298 (2026-10-20): Host != :authority accepted; cache poisoning and host-based ACL bypass. Root cause in every case: two identity derivations (TLS options map vs router host match; :authority vs Host) with different folding (case, wildcard, trailing dot). The CANON-6 fix is one canonical authority value, used for both the TLS options lookup (by SNI, canonicalized with the same function) and routing, and a hard binding check between them.

title: Contrarian axis: reject non-canonical input or normalize it? Evidence on both sides, and why the answer differs for paths/fields (reject) and for browser-facing hosts (WHATWG moved toward permissive)
summary: For rejection: paivana (GNU Taler) proxy commit 4f469917 refuses any request target not already in normal form, because libcurl normalized after the whitelist check ('/assets/../premium/x'); Envoy's edge best practice offers path_with_escaped_slashes_action=REJECT_REQUEST for RFC 3986 clients such as gRPC; Quarkus needed two CVEs (39852 then 50559) because each normalization fix covered one encoding. For normalization: the lighttpd maintainer (#2985) argues that normalizing then forwarding the normalized form is safe and that the real danger is forwarding raw while relying on one's own parse; Cloudflare normalizes at the edge by default, but by default does not forward the normalized form to origin (rules and origin can disagree unless 'normalize to origin' is enabled). The DISA web server SRG (V-264364) says normalize, or reject and close if ambiguity remains. Against strictness for hosts: WHATWG PR #914 relaxed IDNA because strict ToASCII broke real websites. Synthesis: both camps agree on CANON-4 (forward exactly what you checked). Reject is the cheaper way to get it for request targets, which browsers already send canonically. Hosts on ingress need no IDNA at all, because the server matches against its own configured names.
overclaim_risk: The claim that browsers send canonical paths is from the paivana rationale and my reading, not measured here; JS fetch() can send '%2e' and '%2F' verbatim.
underclaim_risk: Envoy's REJECT_REQUEST shows that rejection is deployable at scale for gRPC traffic.

title: Decision: ingress Host/:authority/SNI identity = ASCII-lowercase exact match against the configured A-label vhost set; no IDNA, no Unicode folding, no WHATWG host parser on ingress; IDNA (url 2.5.8) only on egress/SSRF and Origin parsing
summary: Alternatives considered: (a) WHATWG host parse (url crate) on ingress: imports IPv4 shorthand (127.1, 0x7f.0.0.1, 2130706433 -> 127.0.0.1), fullwidth/ideographic-stop folding and the PR #914 drift, none of which a client legitimately needs because browsers send A-labels; (b) UTS-46 idna::domain_to_ascii: 12-24 value disagreements against other parsers on the corpus; (c) raw byte compare without lowercasing: breaks RFC 9110 case-insensitive host; (d) chosen: lowercase ASCII, strip default port, reject trailing dot (or 308 to the dotless form), reject non-ASCII, then exact table lookup; unknown host -> 421 (h2/h3) or 404 (h1). Executed support: the strict host canonicalizer reached 0 disagreement across 7 interpreters on accepted hosts. Reversal condition: a golden deployment that must serve Unicode hosts that some clients send as U-labels in Host (none found).
specifics: Config: vhosts: ["example.com", "xn--fa-hia.de"]; validation at load: each entry must pass canon_host and idna::domain_to_ascii_strict(entry)==entry. TLS SNI is canonicalized by the same function before cert selection. Origin allowlist entries are stored as serialized tuples (scheme, A-label host, port).
overclaim_risk: Rests on the assumption that all clients send A-labels in Host/SNI; true for browsers and curl, not verified for every agent HTTP client.

title: CI gate CANON-DIFF: property test 'authz decision on the canonical form == decision on the form each consumer actually parses' + cross-parser differential over the WPT corpora and a mutation corpus
summary: Gate (cargo test -p aegis-canon --features diff, under heavy.sh in CI). G1 property (proptest, >=100k cases/run): for random raw request parts x generated by a grammar that mixes the attacker operators from the instance ledger (percent-encode any byte, case-flip, insert '/./', '/../', '//', '\\\\', ';', '%2F', '%5C', NBSP/ZWSP/fullwidth, trailing dot, default port, duplicate fields/keys/cookies/params, lone surrogates, big numbers): if canon(x)=Ok(c) then for every consumer P in the golden build (router matchit on c, authz route-id policy, cache-key builder, upstream serializer reparsed by httparse/hyper, handler extractors, serde_json strict codec) decide_authz(c) == decide_authz(P(serialize(c))), and canon(serialize(c)) == c (idempotence). If canon(x)=Reject then no consumer is invoked (checked by a counting mock). G2 differential (deterministic): the WPT urltestdata.json and IdnaTestV2.json pinned by commit hash, plus corpus/corpus.json from this round, are run through every parser present in Cargo.lock that can parse that identity kind (enumerated by xtask from the lockfile: url, http, fluent-uri, cookie, mime, serde_json, httparse). The disagreement table is committed, and any new non-zero cell on CANONICAL inputs fails the build. G3 regression: one test per ledger instance (34 ids) encoding the bypass input -> expected Reject or identical decision. G4 lockfile ban: cargo-deny bans simd-json, sonic-rs (until #481 fixed and duplicate policy configurable) and any second URL parser in the ingress crate graph. G5 Lean/Verus (optional rung): canon_path is a total function over byte strings, small enough for a Verus spec of idempotence and of 'output contains no %2F, %5C, ';', '.', '..', or empty segment'. Acceptance: G1-G4 green on every PR; G1 seed corpus includes all 49+36+25+20+25+20+26 corpus items from this round.
specifics: Harness basis exists: /home/patrickd/aegis/research/state/raw/round-004/07-work/diffh (Rust) + analyze.py + canon_ref.py. Cost estimate: G2 runs in <2 s on the laptop (rust_out.json generation measured at well under 1 s for ~3,900 inputs); G1 at 100k cases is estimated at seconds per identity kind (not measured). Spec freeze: owner table r4e07.owner-table is the interface.
overclaim_risk: Property tests sample the space; the grammar encodes known operators, so it can miss a new class (new Unicode, new spec change like PR #914). The gate shows agreement among the parsers we ship, not with an unknown upstream.
underclaim_risk: Cedar's release process (proof-cedar-lean) found 21 bugs by differential/property testing versus 4 by proofs: DRT is the higher-yield instrument for exactly this kind of spec/impl drift.

title: R-ING-1 flip test: ONE canonicalization owner in the core covers all HTTP-family identity instances with zero per-front-end code; body identities need per-media-type codecs (still core-owned, not per front end); upstream folding needs a per-upstream profile; R-ING-1 moves C -> B for the identity sub-claim
summary: Test: classify each of the 11 instance classes by where its canonicalizer must live. Class (a), request-line/field identity (paths, query, host/authority, SNI binding, header duplicates/case, origin, cookies, media type, gRPC :path): 8 classes, 27 of 34 instances. All of them are produced by the h1/h2/h3 codecs as the same Exchange fields and are canonicalized once, so zero per-front-end code is needed. gRPC, GraphQL, MCP, webhooks and WebSocket upgrade consume the same canonical route/authority/origin (consistent with r3e09.ring1-verdict-amendment). Class (b), body identity (JSON duplicate keys/numbers; would extend to protobuf, form, multipart, XML): it needs one canonical codec per media type in a core codec registry, and both policy and handler use the single parse. That means zero per-front-end code but nonzero per-format code: gRPC needs a protobuf codec whether or not it is a separate front end. Class (c), application identity (tenant/user folding, DB collation): 1 class, 4 instances. It needs typed identifiers (newtype built only by canon_ident) plus bytewise comparison in the DB gate, so it crosses into W-DATA-GATE. Class (d), upstream-specific folding ('/ADMIN', '/admin.', backslash on Windows upstreams): the edge cannot know it, so it is declared per upstream (CANON-8). Verdict: the core-normalization half of R-ING-1 survives, made stronger. The precise form is 'one owner per identity kind, all in the core, plus a per-media-type codec registry and per-upstream profiles', not 'one function'. Evidence grade B: dated instances plus an executed differential that went to 0 after strict canonicalization. It is not A, because no full AEGIS core was built.
specifics: Reversal condition: if a front end needs identity semantics the core cannot express (e.g. HTTP/3 WebTransport session ids, or MCP tool names that need Unicode folding), or if more than 2 identity kinds need per-front-end hooks, per-protocol identity code wins for those kinds.
overclaim_risk: The '27 of 34' classification is my judgment; the instance sample is biased toward HTTP-family CVEs because that is what the search targeted.
underclaim_risk: The executed result is direct evidence that a single strict owner removes disagreement among real parsers; r3 had only 2 instances for the bridge.

title: Implementation-phase spike: measure the false-reject rate of strict canonicalization on real traffic before freezing CANON-2
summary: Not runnable within this explorer's limits (no real traffic corpus). Protocol: (1) take 1M request targets from a public crawl sample (HTTP Archive / Common Crawl WARC request lines) plus the operator's own access logs if any; (2) run canon_path, canon_query, canon_host, canon_cookie_header and canon_media_type; (3) report reject rate per rule (which clause fired), top 20 rejected shapes; (4) for each rule with a reject rate >0.1%, decide between 308-redirect-to-canonical (browsers follow), repair-and-forward-canonical (CANON-4) or keep reject. Expected: path rejects dominated by '//' and trailing-dot/percent-encoded-reserved from bots. Decision informed: whether CANON-2 ships as reject-by-default in the golden, or as redirect for GET/HEAD and reject for unsafe methods.

title: Origin checks must compare parsed (scheme, host, port) tuples from ONE parser against configured tuples; regex and raw-string comparisons fail both ways (2026 CVEs + executed 11/20 raw-vs-parsed disagreements)
summary: 2026 instances: jupyter-server CVE-2026-40110 (unanchored re.match on allow_origin_pat, also reaching WebSocket and login redirect), Litestar CVE-2026-25478 (unescaped '.' in the compiled allowlist). Executed on 20 Origin values with allowlist https://example.com: raw equality vs WHATWG-origin equality disagree on 11 (port 443, case, trailing '/', explicit ':', '?'), WHATWG vs CPython on 3 ('https://example.com\\@evil.com' -> url crate origin example.com but urlsplit host evil.com; fullwidth 'ｅxample.com'; 'example%2ecom'). 'https://example.com.' stays distinct in all parsers (trailing dot is a separate origin; curl CVE-2026-8924 and CVE-2022-30115 show trailing-dot equivalence bugs in the cookie and HSTS stores). Rule (extends l5.origin-audience-session-rules): Origin header must parse with core::canon::origin (strict: no userinfo, no path except empty, no backslash, ASCII host). Serialize it, then compare bytes with an allowlist of serialized origins. Any parse failure -> 403. Never a regex.
